sample_unit: Cobb angles on preoperative whole spine radiographs
models_evaluated: commercially available deep learning Cobb angle measurement software (unnamed)

links.outcome: Cobb angle mean absolute error of AI versus radiology residents against expert consensus ground truth
links.effect: Overall AI MAE 4.57° (95%CI 3.85–5.29), significantly higher than residents (P=0.0017); no significant difference for moderate and severe scoliosis per the conclusion.
links.quote: Overall, the AI's MAE was 4.57° [95%CI 3.85°, 5.29°], significantly higher than that of the residents' (P=0.0017).

links.outcome: AI measurement error by scoliosis severity subgroup (moderate, severe, extreme)
links.effect: For extreme scoliosis, AI MAE was 6.53° (95%CI 5.06–7.86) versus residents' 3.61° (95%CI 3.17–3.97), P<0.001; no significant difference between moderate and severe (P=0.86).
links.quote: For extreme scoliosis, the MAE of the AI (6.53° [95%CI 5.06°, 7.86°]) was significantly higher than that of the residents (3.61° [95%CI, 3.17°, 3.97°]) (P<0.001).

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of a commercially available deep learning tool against radiology residents on spine radiographs without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
